title: BIO 102 ( UNN ) : CHAPTER FIVE ( USES AND TYPES OF ENERGY DERIVED FROM RESPIRATION )
subject: BIO 102

questions.question: Energy is defined as the capacity to do which of the following?
questions.explanation: Energy is defined as the capacity to do work.

questions.question: Which type of energy is described as the energy of motion?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion.

questions.question: Which type of energy is described as stored energy?
questions.explanation: Potential energy is stored energy.

questions.question: The most convenient way of measuring energy is through which form?
questions.explanation: Heat is the most convenient way of measuring energy because all other forms can be converted into heat.

questions.question: Cellular respiration reactions are classified as which type of reactions?
questions.explanation: The reactions involved in respiration are catabolic reactions.

questions.question: Respiration breaks large molecules into smaller ones, releasing energy in the process as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Respiration breaks large molecules into smaller ones, releasing energy in the process as high energy bonds.

questions.question: Cellular respiration is considered which type of redox reaction?
questions.explanation: Cellular respiration is considered an exothermic redox reaction which releases energy.

questions.question: Which molecule is the most common oxidizing agent in respiration?
questions.explanation: The most common oxidizing agent in respiration is molecular oxygen.

questions.question: Nutrients used by animal and plant cells in respiration include sugars, amino acids and which other substance?
questions.explanation: Nutrients commonly used in respiration include sugars, amino acids and fatty acids.

questions.question: Which of the following is a form of energy derived from respiration?
questions.explanation: Respiration provides energy used in different forms including bioluminescence.

questions.question: Bioenergetics is the study of energy changes accompanying which type of reactions?
questions.explanation: Bioenergetics is the study of energy changes accompanying biochemical reactions.

questions.question: The matter within a defined region is called which of the following?
questions.explanation: A system is the matter within a defined region.

questions.question: The matter in the rest of the universe is called which of the following?
questions.explanation: The matter in the rest of the universe is called the surroundings.

questions.question: A system which exchanges matter as well as energy with its surroundings is called which of the following?
questions.explanation: An open system exchanges matter as well as energy with its surroundings.

questions.question: A system which does not exchange matter with the surrounding although it may exchange energy is called which of the following?
questions.explanation: A closed system does not exchange matter with the surrounding although it may exchange energy.

questions.question: The biological system is a closed system maintained at constant what?
questions.explanation: The biological system is a closed system maintained at constant pressure.

questions.question: The first law of thermodynamics states that energy can neither be created nor which of the following?
questions.explanation: The first law of thermodynamics indicates that energy can neither be created nor destroyed.

questions.question: The first law of thermodynamics is expressed mathematically as which of the following?
questions.explanation: The first law of thermodynamics is expressed mathematically as ΔE = Q - W.

questions.question: The change in energy of a system depends on only the initial and final states, and not on which of the following?
questions.explanation: The change in energy of a system depends only on the initial and final states, and not on the path of the transformation.

questions.question: Enthalpy is the heat content of a system which is a function of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Enthalpy is the heat content of a system which is a function of state.

questions.question: The change in enthalpy, ΔH is related to the change in energy, ΔE by which expression?
questions.explanation: The change in enthalpy is related to the change in energy by the expression ΔH = ΔE + PΔV.

questions.question: In biochemical reactions, the volume change, ΔV is small, so ΔH is nearly equal to which of the following?
questions.explanation: The volume change is small for nearly all biochemical reactions and so ΔH is nearly equal to ΔE.

questions.question: The second law of thermodynamics indicates that the universe always tends towards more and more what?
questions.explanation: The second law of thermodynamics indicates that the universe always tends towards more and more disorder.

questions.question: The total entropy of a system and its surroundings must increase if a process is to occur how?
questions.explanation: The total entropy of a system and its surroundings must increase if a process is to occur spontaneously.

questions.question: Equilibrium in a system will result when the randomness or disorder is at what?
questions.explanation: Equilibrium in a system will result when the randomness or disorder is at a maximum.

questions.question: One difficulty in using entropy as a criterion of whether a biochemical process can occur spontaneously is that the entropy changes of chemical reactions are not readily what?
questions.explanation: One difficulty in using entropy as a criterion is that the entropy changes of chemical reactions are not readily measured.

questions.question: Free energy is the component of the total energy of a system which can do what under conditions of constant temperature and pressure?
questions.explanation: Free energy is the component of the total energy of a system which can do work under conditions of constant temperature and pressure.

questions.question: The free energy change, ΔG combines the two laws of thermodynamics, which is expressed basically as which of the following?
questions.explanation: The free energy change combines the two laws of thermodynamics, expressed as ΔG = ΔH - TΔS.

questions.question: If ΔG is negative in sign, the reaction proceeds spontaneously with a loss of energy, meaning it is what?
questions.explanation: If ΔG is negative in sign, the reaction proceeds spontaneously with a loss of energy, meaning it is exergonic.

questions.question: If ΔG is positive, the reaction proceeds only if free energy can be what?
questions.explanation: If ΔG is positive, the reaction proceeds only if free energy can be gained, meaning it is endergonic.

questions.question: If ΔG is zero, the system is at what state?
questions.explanation: If ΔG is zero, the system is at equilibrium and no net change takes place.

questions.question: The rate of a reaction depends on the free energy of activation, while is unrelated to which of the following?
questions.explanation: The rate of a reaction depends on the free energy of activation, which is unrelated to ΔG.

questions.question: The change in free energy, ΔG for a chemical reaction is related to the equilibrium constant of that reaction, which is expressed as which of the following?
questions.explanation: An expression for equilibrium constant may be written as Keq = [C][D]/[A][B].

questions.question: At equilibrium, the expression for free energy change reduces to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Because at equilibrium, ΔG = 0, the expression reduces to ΔG0 = -RT ln Keq.

questions.question: When the equilibrium constant of a reaction is less than unity, the reaction is what?
questions.explanation: When the equilibrium constant of a reaction is less than unity, the reaction is endergonic.

questions.question: When the Keq is greater than 1, the reaction is what?
questions.explanation: When the Keq is greater than 1, the reaction is exergonic.

questions.question: Adenosine triphosphate is the molecular currency or energy currency of what?
questions.explanation: Adenosine triphosphate is the molecular currency or energy currency of the cell.

questions.question: The energy of ATP is stored in the bonds between its terminal what?
questions.explanation: The energy of ATP is stored in the bonds between its terminal phosphate groups.

questions.question: The terminal phosphate groups of ATP repel each other due to their what?
questions.explanation: The terminal phosphate groups repel each other due to their negative charge.

questions.question: Enzymes hydrolyze the terminal phosphate group of ATP to release what?
questions.explanation: Enzymes hydrolyze the terminal phosphate group of ATP to release energy for reactions.

questions.question: If ATP hydrolysis is coupled to an endergonic reaction with a positive ΔG, the two reactions together will be what?
questions.explanation: If ATP hydrolysis is coupled to an endergonic reaction, the two reactions together will be exergonic.

questions.question: ATP is synthesized with energy from which type of reactions?
questions.explanation: ATP is synthesized with energy from exergonic reactions.

questions.question: The sugar present in the structure of ATP is which of the following?
questions.explanation: The sugar present in the structure of ATP is ribose.

questions.question: The nitrogenous base present in the structure of ATP is which of the following?
questions.explanation: The nitrogenous base present in the structure of ATP is adenine.

questions.question: How many phosphate groups are present in a molecule of ATP?
questions.explanation: A molecule of ATP contains three phosphate groups.

questions.question: The bond broken to release energy in ATP is between which groups?
questions.explanation: The bond broken to release energy in ATP is between the terminal phosphate groups.

questions.question: ATP hydrolysis is usually coupled to which type of reactions?
questions.explanation: ATP hydrolysis is usually coupled to endergonic reactions.

questions.question: The cycle of ATP synthesis and hydrolysis is central to which process?
questions.explanation: The cycle of ATP synthesis and hydrolysis is central to metabolism.

questions.question: The standard free energy change is constant for each individual chemical reaction when reactants and products are at what concentration?
questions.explanation: The standard free energy change is constant when reactants and products are at a concentration of 1.0M.

questions.question: In the equation ΔG = ΔG0 + RT ln([C][D]/[A][B]), R stands for which of the following?
questions.explanation: In the equation, R stands for the gas constant.
